rows.selection_reason: With no prior experiments, the most important uncertainty is whether a basic multimodal setup provides a viable performance baseline for this task. config_002 (multimodal, singleprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, concat) is the simplest, most standard multimodal configuration: it uses well-established pretrained encoders (ImageNet ViT-L for images, scVI for RNA), the simplest profile setting (singleprofile), and the simplest fusion (concat), avoiding confounding from aggregation or weighted fusion. This establishes a reference performance against which all more complex multimodal variants (multiprofile, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) and unimodal baselines (image-only, RNA-only) can later be compared. Testing the simplest multimodal setup first is the highest-information use of the first experiment: if it performs well, we validate the multimodal hypothesis and can exploit by exploring which added complexity helps; if it underperforms, we learn that the basic fusion or encoder choice is the bottleneck before investing in more complex configurations.

With only one completed experiment (config_002: multimodal, singleprofile, scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, concat fusion, acc≈0.532), the most fundamental uncertainty is whether multimodal fusion actually adds value over a unimodal baseline. config_005 (image_only, singleprofile, imagenet_vit_l, no aggregation) is the cleanest single-variable comparison to config_002—it removes only the RNA modality while keeping the same image encoder and profile setting. If image-only performs comparably (~0.53), it suggests the RNA signal contributes little and future effort should focus on image representation and aggregation; if it performs substantially worse, it confirms multimodal fusion is worthwhile and justifies further exploration of RNA encoders and fusion strategies. Establishing this unimodal baseline is more informative than testing a second fusion strategy or a different RNA encoder, because it resolves the highest-level design question (is multimodal necessary?) before committing budget to finer-grained comparisons within the multimodal space.

Evidence: config_002 (multimodal, scvi_n200, ViT-L, singleprofile, concat) achieved 0.532 acc, while config_005 (image_only, ViT-L, singleprofile) achieved only 0.227 acc. This large gap suggests RNA carries most of the signal, but we cannot yet quantify how much of the multimodal performance comes from RNA alone versus the image modality. Question: config_008 (rna_only, singleprofile, scvi_n200) isolates the RNA contribution by removing the image modality while keeping the same RNA encoder and profile setting as config_002. If RNA-only ≈ 0.53, the image adds little and future effort should focus on RNA encoder/aggregation choices; if RNA-only is substantially lower, the image modality is genuinely complementary and fusion strategy becomes a high-value design axis. Why this is the best next experiment: it is the single most informative ablation given only two completed runs—it resolves the fundamental uncertainty about modality contribution with a minimal, controlled change (only model_setting differs from config_002), and its result will most efficiently direct all subsequent experiments under the limited budget.

Evidence: config_002 (multimodal, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, concat) achieved 0.532 acc, only marginally above RNA-alone scvi_n200 (0.520), while image-alone was very weak (0.227). This suggests the RNA encoder is the dominant signal source and the image contributes little. Uncertainty: we have only tested one RNA encoder (scvi_n200); it is unknown whether scgpt produces a more informative representation that could raise the ceiling. Question: config_023 changes exactly one variable relative to config_002 (RNA encoder scvi_n200 → scgpt) while holding model_setting, profile_setting, image_encoder, aggregation, and fusion constant. This cleanly isolates the effect of the RNA representation. Why best next: the RNA encoder is the highest-leverage design choice given that RNA drives most of the signal; a single-variable comparison against our current best (config_002) maximizes information per experiment and avoids confounding with fusion or image-encoder changes. If scgpt substantially outperforms scvi_n200, it redirects the search toward scgpt-based configurations; if not, it confirms scvi_n200 is adequate and we can pivot to fusion or profile-setting questions.

Evidence: config_002 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, concat, singleprofile) achieves 0.532 acc, barely above rna_only (0.520), indicating the image modality contributes very little under concat fusion. scvi_n200 clearly outperforms scgpt (~10 pt gap). The key uncertainty is whether the near-zero image contribution is due to the fusion mechanism (concat vs. weighted) or to the image representation itself. Question tested: config_051 is identical to config_002 except fusion changes from concat to weighted, isolating the effect of fusion strategy on how much the image modality can contribute. Why best next experiment: it is a clean single-variable comparison from the current best configuration, directly tests whether a better fusion mechanism can unlock image value, and the answer (weighted helps or not) will determine whether subsequent budget should go toward multiprofile/aggregation (if fusion was the bottleneck) or toward a different image encoder (if the image features are inherently weak). This maximizes information gain per experiment under the limited budget.

Evidence: scvi_n200 is clearly the superior RNA encoder (0.520 rna_only vs 0.435 multimodal with scgpt), weighted fusion slightly edges out concat (0.537 vs 0.532), and the image modality adds a small but real benefit over RNA-only (~1.2%). However, we have only tested imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder. Uncertainty: it is unknown whether resnet50 would match, exceed, or underperform imagenet_vit_l in the multimodal setting, and this choice will affect the final configuration. Question: config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, weighted fusion) is a clean single-variable swap of the image encoder relative to our best result (config_051, same but imagenet_vit_l). This isolates the image-encoder effect while holding the RNA encoder, profile setting, and fusion strategy at their best-supported values. Rationale: Under a tight budget, this is the highest-information next step because it (a) builds on our strongest evidence, (b) changes only one variable to cleanly attribute any performance shift to the image encoder, and (c) directly informs whether we should invest remaining budget in resnet50-based or ViT-based multimodal pipelines for subsequent multiprofile/aggregation experiments.

All six completed experiments use singleprofile with no aggregation, leaving the multiprofile+aggregation dimension completely untested. The best result so far is config_016 (scvi_n200, resnet50, weighted, singleprofile; acc=0.540). The small multimodal gain over RNA-only (~1-2%) suggests the current single-profile setup may be underutilizing available information. config_028 directly extends the best configuration by switching to multiprofile with avgpool aggregation while keeping the same encoders (scvi_n200, resnet50) and fusion (weighted). This isolates the effect of multiprofile+aggregation with the simplest, most robust aggregation method, avoiding the confound of simultaneously introducing a more complex transformer aggregator. If it improves on 0.540, we gain evidence that multi-profile information is valuable and can then explore transformer aggregation; if not, we learn that added complexity is not warranted, saving budget from pursuing that direction.

Evidence: config_028 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieved the best performance (acc=0.678, F1=0.646), showing that multiprofile with avgpool aggregation provides a ~14-point boost over singleprofile. However, we have only tested avgpool aggregation in the multiprofile setting; the effect of transformer aggregation remains untested. Question: config_045 is identical to config_028 except aggregation changes from avgpool to transformer (all other settings: multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, weighted). This isolates the effect of aggregation strategy in the most promising configuration family. Why this is the best next experiment: It is a clean single-variable comparison against our current best, directly testing whether a more expressive aggregation (transformer) can further improve over simple avgpool. Given the limited budget, confirming or ruling out transformer aggregation in the top-performing setup is the highest-information experiment before exploring other dimensions (image encoder, fusion, RNA encoder variants).

The current best (config_045: multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted; acc=0.713) shows that multiprofile + transformer aggregation is the dominant driver of performance. However, in singleprofile, RNA alone (0.520) was nearly as strong as multimodal (0.532–0.540), while image-only was very weak (0.227), suggesting the image modality contributes little. The critical open question is whether this pattern holds in the multiprofile+transformer regime, where cross-modal interaction dynamics may differ. config_024 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) is a clean one-variable ablation of the image modality from the current best. If it approaches ~0.70, the image modality is redundant and future effort should focus on RNA encoder and aggregation refinements; if it drops substantially, the image modality becomes essential in multiprofile and we should optimize the image encoder. This single experiment resolves a fundamental design decision (is multimodality needed?) that will shape all remaining budget allocation, making it the highest-information experiment available.

The current best (config_045: 0.713 acc) uses resnet50 as the image encoder in a multiprofile + transformer + weighted fusion setting. The only prior evidence on image encoder choice comes from singleprofile experiments (config_016 resnet50: 0.540 vs config_051 imagenet_vit_l: 0.537), where the difference was small and the regime was fundamentally different (no multiprofile aggregation). config_038 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) is a clean single-variable comparison against config_045, isolating the effect of image encoder in the high-performing multiprofile + transformer regime. This is critical because the image encoder determines the quality of the visual representation being fused, and confirming whether resnet50's advantage persists (or reverses) when paired with transformer aggregation will guide all subsequent multimodal experiments. Under the limited budget, this is the highest-information exploitation step: it either validates the current best's encoder choice (allowing us to fix that variable) or reveals a better encoder that could push performance further.
